title: Reservoir throttle and degraded-response orchestration for safe model fallback
creator: Emily Chen
description: Implement a reservoir-based throttle and degraded-response orchestration that provides per-dependency / per-model / per-tenant isolation, deterministic trip logic, and automated safe fallbacks that preserve SLOs and customer experience during overload and cross-region failure scenarios.
background: Current trip implementations are mostly hysteresis-based with single-window thresholds. We need a mechanism that absorbs short spikes without full trips, enforces proportional load shedding when saturation persists, and provides graceful degraded responses (with fallback model routing, cached prefixes, or structured errors) while preserving important SLAs (p99 latency and availability targets). This is especially important for multi-region failover where transient surges occur during reroutes.
proposal_summary: Build a two-tier circuit: a short-term reservoir (burst absorber) and a long-term dampener (sustained load detector). The reservoir allows brief bursts without tripping; the dampener measures sustained violations and triggers progressive degradation policies. Degradation options include traffic redirection to cheaper model variants, synthetic-brevity responses, cached-prefix resolution, and coordinated regional spillover. All actions are observable and reversible with clear rollback hooks.
design_decisions: Use reservoir (leaky-bucket) sized relative to baseline qps per tenant/dependency to avoid global trips from short spikes.
Dampener uses EWMA of error-rate and latency over a 5-10 minute window to detect sustained issues.
Trip semantics are graduated: soft trip (probabilistic shedding) -> hard trip (reroute + degraded responses) -> quarantine (traffic cut for extreme cases).
Fallbacks prefer semantically compatible model variants first (same family, quantized), then cached outputs, then structured degraded responses. No silent failures.
Expose configuration at three tiers: global defaults, per-model overrides, per-tenant overrides with safe upper/lower bounds.
All policy changes are controlled via Console rollouts (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic safety rollback on metric regressions.
Metrics are emitted at token-level and request-level: reservoir_fill, shed_rate, reroute_rate, fallback_type, p50/p95/p99 latency, gpu_util, queued_requests.
Keep decision logic centralized for consistency but implement lightweight local enforcement in edge proxies for latency-sensitive reactions.
Security review: no user data is modified in fallback paths; logging respects PII rules and KMS-encrypted audit logs are kept for incidents.
metrics: Model GPU utilization and KV-cache hit rate
Region failover churn and cross-region latency delta
trip_thresholds: Short-term reservoir: capacity = max(ceil(0.25 * baseline_tps), 50 requests) for 30s; exceeding reservoir leads to soft-shed probability proportional to overfill.
Soft trip: short-window error-rate > 5% OR p95 latency > 3x baseline for 60s => enable probabilistic shedding (start at 5% up to 50%).
Hard trip: sustained EWMA error-rate > 10% for 5m OR reservoir overfill > 400% for 3m => reroute to fallback path and enable degraded-response generator.
Quarantine: uncorrected hard trip beyond 15m escalates to traffic cut with manual review; tenants with safety-critical flags have stricter thresholds (lower tolerance).
Per-model overrides: models marked 'low-quality-allowed' can be shed earlier to preserve premium workloads.
fallback_behavior: Tier 1: route to compatible quantized variant in same region with fastest-safe lateral failover.
Tier 2: serve cached prefix completions if KV-cache hit exists (attach 'stale: true' metadata).
Tier 3: use degraded-response generator that returns structured short-form answers with provenance header and an 'is_degraded' flag.
Tier 4: probabilistic queue admission where a small fraction of requests are allowed through to primary path for sampling/QA.
Audit: every fallback includes a telemetry envelope pointing to the trigger metric and policy that executed, for downstream SLO reconciliation.
Cross-region spillover: if primary region capacity is saturated and network latency to fallback region < configured threshold, gradually shift traffic with weighted routing and a 10-minute cooldown.
No silent fallback: client receives explicit response code and header so SDKs/servers can opt-in to retry strategies.
Fail open safety: if fallback routes also fail, system returns a safe error with human-readable guidance (retry-after, degraded capabilities).
rollout_plan: Unit tests + integration harness simulating reservoir overfills and regional failovers (local CI).
Internal canary: enable policy for internal-only tenants + synthetic traffic for 24h.
Gradual customer canary: 1% traffic on non-critical tenants for 4h, monitor primary metrics and rollback on any p99 regression > 10%.
Progress to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with automated metric gating.
Post-rollout: 7 day observation window and a retro with runbook updates.
tests: Simulate burst scenarios with varied spike shapes (10s, 1m, 5m) and validate reservoir absorption without false hard trips.
Chaos test: simulate regional link flaps and verify spillover and rebalancing safety with no SLO regression for premium tenants.
Regression: ensure no increased tail latency when reservoir is disabled vs enabled for baseline traffic.
E2E: verify telemetry envelopes include fallback_type and trigger_metric for downstream analysis.
Load test with mixed-tenancy: ensure per-tenant isolation prevents noisy neighbor trips.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics are visible in Console dashboards and match synthetic ground truth within 5%.
Soft-shed path reduces primary p99 latency by at least 20% in sustained overload tests while keeping availability above SLOs for premium tenants.
Fallback responses include headers and telemetry and are retrievable in logs for at least 30 days.
No customer-facing regressions during canary phases; rollback procedures validated.
Runbook updated with triage steps and emergency rollback commands.
